claims.text: The identity of X governs protective-oxide stability in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Al promotes formation of an ultrastable, slow-growing, coherent Al2O3 layer.
The Al2O3 layer has low ionic diffusivity.
The thermal expansion coefficient of the Al2O3 layer is closer to that of the HEA substrate than those of the oxides produced by Si- or Mn-bearing alloys.
Low ionic diffusivity and favorable thermal-expansion matching keep Al2O3 interfacial stress below the threshold for crack initiation.
Si or Mn promotes rapidly growing, discontinuous oxide scales.
Oxides formed on the Si- or Mn-bearing alloys have higher diffusivity than the Al2O3 scale.
Oxides formed on the Si- or Mn-bearing alloys have greater thermal-expansion mismatch with their substrates.
Rapid oxide growth and thermal-expansion mismatch cause stress accumulation, cracking, and eventual spallation.
Oxide grain size and oxide/alloy interface quality mediate stress transfer and scale adhesion.
At 950 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for up to 100 hours, only CrFeCoNiAl will retain a coherent, adherent, slow-growing protective scale.
Under the same exposure, CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn will show rapid oxide growth, interfacial cracking, and spallation.
There is a compositional threshold at which increasing Al content improves oxide integrity.
The comparison will use initially single-phase, homogenized CrFeCoNiX alloys prepared by arc melting and homogenization.
The alloys will be compared under nominally identical oxidation and processing conditions so that X is the principal varied factor.
Temperature, atmosphere, and alloy microstructure outside the specified boundaries may alter oxide behavior.

contradictions.description: The intervention and conditions state that effects can be attributed purely to composition, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that uncontrolled differences in grain size and phase homogeneity could influence oxidation behavior.
The baseline is described as behavior in the absence of compositional alterations, but the actual comparison changes X among Al, Si, and Mn; no separate fixed-composition or no-X baseline is defined.
